| Periodic recording                                                                           | With this release, AWS Config supports periodic recording. Periodic recording<br>provides you with the ability to capture the latest configuration changes for<br>your resources over a fixed period of time. You can now set the default<br>frequency for the configuration recorder to Daily, allowing you to receive a<br>configuration item (CI) representing the most recent state of your resources<br>over the last 24-hour period, only if it’s different from the previous CI<br>recorded. The AWS Config console also introduces a new recording strategy experience,<br>where you can also override the recording frequency for specific resource types<br>or exclude specific resource types from recording. This can help make your<br>settings fit your granular requirements.The following data types are added:<br>• [RecordingMode](../APIReference/API_RecordingMode.md "../APIReference/API_RecordingMode.md")<br>• [RecordingModeOverride](../APIReference/API_RecordingModeOverride.md "../APIReference/API_RecordingModeOverride.md")<br>The following data types are updated:<br>• [PutConfigurationRecorder](../APIReference/API_PutConfigurationRecorder.md "../APIReference/API_PutConfigurationRecorder.md")<br>• [ConfigurationRecorder](../APIReference/API_ConfigurationRecorder.md "../APIReference/API_ConfigurationRecorder.md")<br>• [BaseConfigurationItem](../APIReference/API_BaseConfigurationItem.md "../APIReference/API_BaseConfigurationItem.md")<br>• [ConfigurationItem](../APIReference/API_ConfigurationItem.md "../APIReference/API_ConfigurationItem.md")<br>The following pages in the developer guide are updated:<br>• [Recoding AWS<br>Resources](select-resources.md "select-resources.md")<br>• [Setting up AWS Config with<br>the AWS Config Console You can use this feature to concentrate on<br>critical resources that are subject to your compliance and governance<br>standards.The updates to the API for the configuration recorder and recording group<br>are backward compatible, meaning that they work with previous versions of<br>the [PutConfigurationRecorder](../APIReference/API_PutConfigurationRecorder.md "../APIReference/API_PutConfigurationRecorder.md") API. "../APIReference/API_ExclusionByResourceTypes.md")<br>The following data types are updated:<br>• [PutConfigurationRecorder](../APIReference/API_PutConfigurationRecorder.md "../APIReference/API_PutConfigurationRecorder.md")<br>• [ConfigurationRecorder](../APIReference/API_ConfigurationRecorder.md "../APIReference/API_ConfigurationRecorder.md")<br>• [RecordingGroup](../APIReference/API_RecordingGroup.md "../APIReference/API_RecordingGroup.md")<br>The following page in the developer guide is updated:<br>• [Selecting Which<br>Resources are Recorded](select-resources.md "select-resources.md") | Drift Detection as Configuration Item (CI) for the AWS Config Configuration<br>Recorder      | With this release, AWS Config tracks all changes to the configuration recorder to<br>indicate if the state of the configuration recorder differs, or has<br>_drifted_, from its previous state; for example, if there<br>are updates to resource types that you have enabled AWS Config to track, if you have<br>stopped or started the configuration recorder, or if you have deleted or<br>uninstalled the configuration recorder. The<br>`AWS::Config::ConfigurationRecorder` resource type is a system<br>resource type of AWS Config and recording of this resource type is enabled by default<br>in all supported Regions. Recording for the<br>`AWS::Config::ConfigurationRecorder` resource type comes with no<br>additional charge. For more information, see [Drift Detection<br>for the Configuration Recorder](stop-start-recorder.md#drift-detection "stop-start-recorder.md#drift-detection"). | Compliance score for conformance packs                                                       | With this release, AWS Config introduces compliance score for conformance packs,<br>which provides you with a high-level view of the compliance state of your<br>conformance packs. You can use it to identify, investigate, and understand the<br>level of compliance in your conformance packs. A compliance score is the<br>percentage of the number of compliant rule-resource combinations in a<br>conformance pack compared to the number of total possible rule-resource<br>combinations in the conformance pack.The following data types are updated:<br>• [ListConformancePackComplianceScores](../APIReference/API_ListConformancePackComplianceScores.md "../APIReference/API_ListConformancePackComplianceScores.md")<br>• [ConformancePackComplianceScore](../APIReference/API_ConformancePackComplianceScore.md "../APIReference/API_ConformancePackComplianceScore.md")<br>The following pages in the developer guide are updated:<br>• [Viewing the AWS Config Dashboard](viewing-the-aws-config-dashboard.md "viewing-the-aws-config-dashboard.md")<br>• [Viewing<br>Compliance Data in the Conformance Packs<br>Dashboard](conformance-pack-dashboard.md "conformance-pack-dashboard.md")<br>• [Managing<br>Conformance Packs (API)](conformance-pack-apis.md "conformance-pack-apis.md") | AWS Config Integration with AWS Security Hub CSPM                                            | With this release, you can see the results of AWS Config managed and custom rule<br>evaluations as findings in AWS Security Hub CSPM. Security Hub CSPM transforms rule evaluations into<br>findings, which provide more information about the impacted resources, such as<br>the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) and creation date. These findings can be viewed<br>alongside other Security Hub CSPM findings, providing a comprehensive overview of your<br>security posture. For more information, see [Sending Rule Evaluations to Security Hub CSPM](evaluate-config_manage-rules.md#setting-up-aws-config-rules-with-console-integration "evaluate-config_manage-rules.md#setting-up-aws-config-rules-with-console-integration") | AWS Config Custom Policy rules                                                               | With this release, AWS Config allows you to create AWS Config Custom Policy rules using<br>AWS CloudFormation Guard ([guard](https://github.com/aws-cloudformation/cloudformation-guard "https://github.com/aws-cloudformation/cloudformation-guard")). Guard is a policy-as-code language that allows you to write<br>policies that are enforced by AWS Config without the need to create Lambda functions<br>to manage your custom rules. Rules written using Guard policy can be created<br>from the AWS Config console or by using the AWS Config rule APIs.The following pages in the developer guide are updated:<br>• [AWS Config<br>Custom Rules](evaluate-config_develop-rules.md "evaluate-config_develop-rules.md")<br>• [Creating AWS Config Custom Rules with Guard](evaluate-config_develop-rules_cfn-guard.md "evaluate-config_develop-rules_cfn-guard.md")<br>The following data types are updated:<br>• [Source](../APIReference/API_Source.md "../APIReference/API_Source.md")<br>• [CustomPolicyDetails](../APIReference/API_CustomPolicyDetails.md "../APIReference/API_CustomPolicyDetails.md")<br>• [ConfigRuleEvaluationStatus](../APIReference/API_ConfigRuleEvaluationStatus.md "../APIReference/API_ConfigRuleEvaluationStatus.md")<br>• [GetCustomRulePolicy](../APIReference/API_GetCustomRulePolicy.md "../APIReference/API_GetCustomRulePolicy.md")<br>• [GetOrganizationCustomRulePolicy](../APIReference/API_GetOrganizationCustomRulePolicy.md "../APIReference/API_GetOrganizationCustomRulePolicy.md")<br>• [OrganizationCustomPolicyRuleMetadata](../APIReference/API_OrganizationCustomPolicyRuleMetadata.md "../APIReference/API_OrganizationCustomPolicyRuleMetadata.md") | Changes to Global Resource Type Recording                                                    | AWS Config now changes how new global resource types are recorded in AWS Config Recording.<br>Global resource types are AWS resources that do not require you to specify a<br>region at creation. Before this change, you could enable the recording of global<br>resource types in all supported regions in AWS Config. After this change, new global<br>resource types onboarded to AWS Config recording can only be recorded in the service's<br>home region for the commercial partition, and AWS GovCloud (US-West) for the<br>AWS GovCloud (US) partition. You will now be able to view the configuration items<br>for these new global resource types only in their home region and<br>AWS GovCloud (US-West). For a list of home regions for global resource types<br>onboarded after February 2022, see the table on the [Recording All<br>Supported Resource Types](select-resources.md#select-resources-all "select-resources.md#select-resources-all") page. This policy also now grants permission to<br>retrieve the specified alternate contact attached to an AWS account, retrieve<br>information about an AWS Organizations policy, retrieve an Amazon ECR repository policy,<br>retrieve information about an archived AWS Config rule, retrieve a list of Amazon ECS task<br>definition families, list the root or parent organizational units (OUs) of the<br>specified child OU or account, and list the policies that are attached to the<br>specified target root, organizational unit, or account. For more information,<br>see [AWS managed policies<br>for AWS Config](security-iam-awsmanpol.md "security-iam-awsmanpol.md").
